title: Near-complete genome sequences of five norovirus GII.4[P31] strains from coastal Kenya, 2019
abstract: ABSTRACT There is limited norovirus genomic data from Africa. We report five near-complete norovirus genomes of genotype GII.4[P31], recovered from stool samples of children admitted with acute diarrhea in coastal Kenya during 2019. These expand the available genomic data resource for norovirus evolutionary studies, molecular assay improvement, and therapeutics development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of genomic data on norovirus in Africa, which is critical for understanding its epidemiology and evolution in the region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the recovery of five near-complete norovirus genomes from stool samples of children with acute diarrhea in coastal Kenya during 2019.
analysis.methods: The researchers sequenced the genomes to expand the genomic data resource for norovirus evolutionary studies, molecular assay improvement, and therapeutics development.
analysis.main_results: Five near-complete norovirus genomes of genotype GII.4[P31] were successfully recovered from the stool samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide new genomic data for norovirus in Africa, contributing to the understanding of its genetic diversity and evolution in the region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The data can inform surveillance efforts and improve molecular assays for norovirus detection in Africa, which is essential for public health preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the sequencing of five near-complete norovirus GII.4[P31] genomes from children with acute diarrhea in coastal Kenya during 2019. The research was motivated by the limited genomic data on norovirus in Africa, which hampers understanding of its epidemiology and evolution. The study expands the genomic resource for norovirus, offering insights into genetic diversity and potential for molecular assay improvement. The findings are significant for surveillance and public health in the region, though the small sample size limits broader generalizability. The evidence is strong due to the direct sequencing of the viral genomes, which provides reliable data for further research.

title: Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance for monitoring human norovirus GII circulation
abstract: Norovirus GII causes a substantial global burden of acute gastroenteritis, and genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance offers a complementary approach for monitoring community circulation beyond cases captured by routine clinical surveillance. We monitored four municipal wastewater treatment plants in Beijing, China, from October 2023 to September 2024 and compared weekly GII genotype profiles with contemporaneous sporadic-case and outbreak surveillance. Strict-weekly genotype comparisons were the primary inference and used moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals, block-sign tests, and false-discovery-rate correction; centred 3-week profiles were used for description and sensitivity analysis. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity quantified compositional concordance, and same-week and lagged Spearman correlations compared wastewater GII concentration with clinical surveillance activity. In the centred 3-week wastewater series, GII.4 had the highest mean read-based relative abundance (31.1%), followed by GII.17 (17.5%) and GII.7 (15.2%). In strict-weekly comparisons, wastewater had lower GII.17 representation than sporadic cases (-32.6 percentage points) and lower GII.7 representation than outbreaks (-14.0 percentage points). Wastewater had higher GII.3, GII.4, GII.6, and GII.9 representation than sporadic cases and higher GII.9 and GII.13 representation than outbreaks; the GII.4 and GII.7 differences were sensitive to analytical specification, and the GII.13 effect was small. Mean strict-weekly Bray-Curtis dissimilarities were 0.590-0.679 in 32 common weeks. Same-week and lagged wastewater concentration correlations with sporadic-case positivity and outbreak case counts were not significant after temporal-dependence and multiplicity correction. Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance documented co-circulating GII genotypes and recurrent source-specific differences, while read-based relative abundance remained dependent on catchment coverage and genotype-specific analytical performance.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to monitor the circulation of human norovirus GII genotypes using genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance, complementing routine clinical data. Four wastewater treatment plants in Beijing were monitored from October 2023 to September 2024, with weekly GII genotype profiles compared to sporadic-case and outbreak surveillance. The methods involved strict-weekly comparisons using statistical techniques like moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals and false-discovery-rate correction, alongside centred 3-week profiles for sensitivity analysis. The main results showed that GII.4 had the highest mean read-based relative abundance in wastewater, followed by GII.17 and GII.7. In strict-weekly comparisons, wastewater had lower GII.17 and GII.7 representation than sporadic cases and outbreaks, respectively. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of co-circulating GII genotypes and source-specific differences, highlighting the utility of wastewater surveillance for tracking norovirus circulation. The study's significance lies in its potential to improve surveillance strategies for norovirus, while its limitations include non-significant correlations between wastewater concentrations and clinical data after statistical corrections.

title_zh: 基于基因型的污水监测用于追踪人类急性胃肠炎诺如病毒GII的流行情况
source_body_en: Norovirus GII causes a substantial global burden of acute gastroenteritis, and genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance offers a complementary approach for monitoring community circulation beyond cases captured by routine clinical surveillance. We monitored four municipal wastewater treatment plants in Beijing, China, from October 2023 to September 2024 and compared weekly GII genotype profiles with contemporaneous sporadic-case and outbreak surveillance. Strict-weekly genotype comparisons were the primary inference and used moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals, block-sign tests, and false-discovery-rate correction; centred 3-week profiles were used for description and sensitivity analysis. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity quantified compositional concordance, and same-week and lagged Spearman correlations compared wastewater GII concentration with clinical surveillance activity. In the centred 3-week wastewater series, GII.4 had the highest mean read-based relative abundance (31.1%), followed by GII.17 (17.5%) and GII.7 (15.2%). In strict-weekly comparisons, wastewater had lower GII.17 representation than sporadic cases (-32.6 percentage points) and lower GII.7 representation than outbreaks (-14.0 percentage points). Wastewater had higher GII.3, GII.4, GII.6, and GII.9 representation than sporadic cases and higher GII.9 and GII.13 representation than outbreaks; the GII.4 and GII.7 differences were sensitive to analytical specification, and the GII.13 effect was small. Mean strict-weekly Bray-Curtis dissimilarities were 0.590-0.679 in 32 common weeks. Same-week and lagged wastewater concentration correlations with sporadic-case positivity and outbreak case counts were not significant after temporal-dependence and multiplicity correction. Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance documented co-circulating GII genotypes and recurrent source-specific differences, while read-based relative abundance remained dependent on catchment coverage and genotype-specific analytical performance.
abstract_zh: 诺如病毒GII导致了全球范围内的急性胃肠炎重大负担,而基于基因型的污水监测提供了一种补充方法,用于监测社区传播情况,超越了常规临床监测所捕捉的病例。我们在中国北京监测了四个市政污水诺如病毒处理厂,时间从2023年10月至2024年9月,并将每周的GII基因型谱与同期的零星病例和诺如病毒监测数据进行比较。严格的每周基因型比较是主要推断方法,使用移动块自举置信区间、块符号检验和错误发现率校正;以中心3周的谱型用于描述和敏感性分析。Bray-Curtis差异度量化了组成一致性,而同期和滞后Spearman相关性比较了污水中GII浓度与临床监测活动。在中心3周的污水系列中,GII.4具有最高的平均基于读数的相对丰度(31.1%),其次是GII.17(17.5%)和GII.7(15.2%)。在严格每周比较中,污水中GII.17的代表性低于零星病例(-32.6个百分点),污水中GII.7的代表性低于诺如病毒(-14.0个百分点)。污水中GII.3、GII.4、GII.6和GII.9的代表性高于零星病例,且GII.9和GII.13的代表性高于诺如病毒;GII.4和GII.7的差异对分析参数敏感,而GII.13的影响较小。在32个共同周中,严格每周的Bray-Curtis差异度平均为0.590-0.679。在时间依赖性和多重性校正后,污水浓度与零星病例阳性率和诺如病毒病例数的同期和滞后相关性均不显著。基于基因型的污水监测记录了共循环的GII基因型和反复出现的来源特异性差异,而基于读数的相对丰度仍依赖于排水区域覆盖范围和基因型特异性分析性能。

title: Bile and capsid variation coregulate histo-blood group antigen recognition and serum neutralization potency in GII.12 human norovirus
abstract: ABSTRACT Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. GII strains cause the majority of HuNoV outbreaks globally, with host susceptibility influenced by genetic polymorphisms that regulate mucosal expression of histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding ligands. HuNoV viral capsid (VP1) diversity in residues adjacent to the conserved HBGA binding pocket selectively stabilizes ligand interactions. Additionally, select HuNoV capsids demonstrate bile-influenced conformational plasticity, further enabling HBGA engagement. Combined, these factors have the potential to enhance the breadth of binding of HuNoV to HBGAs, driving population susceptibility. Here we characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. Mutational analysis demonstrated amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis demonstrated minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons demonstrated variable impacts of bile. Bile improved GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA, in contrast to GII.4, GII.3, and GII.6. Further, bile reduced surrogate neutralizing antibody potency for GII.2 and GII.12 but not GII.4 and GII.6 strains. Collectively, these studies suggest that HuNoV bile-dependence is not a general feature of GII norovirus, but instead can be genotype or strain specific. These data inform how select GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, providing potential mechanistic evidence for continual viral circulation. IMPORTANCE Human norovirus-host interactions are complex, influenced by viral diversity, host-ligand expression profiles, and the gastrointestinal environment. Periodically, outbreaks of endemic human noroviruses, like GII.12, demonstrate genetic diversity between viral strains of a genotype. Exploring this, two GII.12 outbreak strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on the viral capsid ligand and antibody binding. Residue changes between the two strains modulated affinity for histo-blood group antigens that could be compensated for by addition of bile. Although bile improved HBGA-binding, it reduced serum and monoclonal antibody neutralization potency to GII.12. These observations demonstrate the balanced impact of bile-mediated viral capsid conformational plasticity in ligand recognition and potential immune evasion for select GII genotypes. Bile had similar effects for GII.2 HuNoV, but did not impact GII.6 or GII.4 HuNoV HBGA-binding and serum-ligand blocking potency, indicating that GII HuNoV strains potentially utilize multiple mechanisms to ensure host breadth and antigenic diversity.

analysis.methods: Mutational analysis was used to assess the impact of amino acid changes at VP1 positions 373 and 392 on HBGA ligand binding. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on two GII.12 strains, which may not represent the full genetic diversity of GII.12 HuNoV. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on mutational and serological analyses of a limited set of strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how capsid variation and bile influence histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) recognition and serum neutralization potency in GII.12 human norovirus (HuNoV). The research highlights that amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA binding, and that bile can enhance HBGA engagement but reduce neutralizing antibody potency for GII.12 strains. These findings suggest that bile-mediated conformational changes in the viral capsid may contribute to immune evasion and the continued circulation of GII.12 HuNoV. The study provides insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying host susceptibility and immune response to specific GII genotypes, which could inform future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. However, the study is limited by its focus on a small number of strains, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

title_zh: 胆汁和衣壳变异共同调控组胺血型抗原识别和血清中和能力在GII.12人类诺如病毒中
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. GII strains cause the majority of HuNoV outbreaks globally, with host susceptibility influenced by genetic polymorphisms that regulate mucosal expression of histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding ligands. HuNoV viral capsid (VP1) diversity in residues adjacent to the conserved HBGA binding pocket selectively stabilizes ligand interactions. Additionally, select HuNoV capsids demonstrate bile-influenced conformational plasticity, further enabling HBGA engagement. Combined, these factors have the potential to enhance the breadth of binding of HuNoV to HBGAs, driving population susceptibility. Here we characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. Mutational analysis demonstrated amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis demonstrated minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons demonstrated variable impacts of bile. Bile improved GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA, in contrast to GII.4, GII.3, and GII.6. Further, bile reduced surrogate neutralizing antibody potency for GII.2 and GII.12 but not GII.4 and GII.6 strains. Collectively, these studies suggest that HuNoV bile-dependence is not a general feature of GII norovirus, but instead can be genotype or strain specific. These data inform how select GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, providing potential mechanistic evidence for continual viral circulation. IMPORTANCE Human norovirus-host interactions are complex, influenced by viral diversity, host-ligand expression profiles, and the gastrointestinal environment. Periodically, outbreaks of endemic human noroviruses, like GII.12, demonstrate genetic diversity between viral strains of a genotype. Exploring this, two GII.12 outbreak strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on the viral capsid ligand and antibody binding. Residue changes between the two strains modulated affinity for histo-blood group antigens that could be compensated for by addition of bile. Although bile improved HBGA-binding, it reduced serum and monoclonal antibody neutralization potency to GII.12. These observations demonstrate the balanced impact of bile-mediated viral capsid conformational plasticity in ligand recognition and potential immune evasion for select GII genotypes. Bile had similar effects for GII.2 HuNoV, but did not impact GII.6 or GII.4 HuNoV HBGA-binding and serum-ligand blocking potency, indicating that GII HuNoV strains potentially utilize multiple mechanisms to ensure host breadth and antigenic diversity.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)是急性胃肠炎的主要病因之一,年轻儿童和老年人承担着最大的疾病负担。GII型株在全球范围内导致了大多数HuNoV感染,其易感性受到调控黏膜表达组胺血型抗原(HBGA)结合配体的遗传多态性的影响。HuNoV病毒衣壳(VP1)在保守的HBGA结合位点附近的残基多样性可选择性稳定配体相互作用。此外,某些HuNoV衣壳表现出胆汁影响的构象可塑性,进一步促进HBGA的结合。综上所述,这些因素可能增强HuNoV对HBGA的结合范围,从而驱动人群易感性。在这里,我们表征了两种同时共循环的GII.12 暴发株,它们在五个关键VP1位点上存在差异。突变分析表明,VP1位点373和392的氨基酸共同调控HBGA配体结合。血清学分析表明,这些位点的抗原性影响较小。更广泛的GII比较显示胆汁对HBGA结合的影响存在差异。胆汁增强了GII.2和GII.12对HBGA的结合,但对GII.4、GII.3和GII.6则没有这种效果。此外,胆汁降低了GII.2和GII.12的替代中和抗体效力,但对GII.4和GII.6株则没有影响。总体而言,这些研究结果表明,HuNoV对胆汁的依赖性并不是GII 诺如病毒的普遍特征,而是可能与基因型或菌株特异性相关。这些数据有助于理解某些GII HuNoV菌株如何调节与组胺血型抗原配体和免疫识别相关的衣壳残基,为病毒持续传播提供了潜在的机制证据。重要性 人类诺如病毒与组胺血型抗原的相互作用是复杂的,受到病毒多样性、组胺血型抗原配体表达谱以及胃肠道环境的影响。有时,流行性人类诺如病毒,如GII.12,其病毒株之间会表现出基因型内的遗传多样性。本研究通过使用两种GII.12 暴发菌株来模拟遗传变化对病毒衣壳配体和抗体结合的影响。两种菌株之间的残基变化调节了对组胺血型抗原的亲和力,这种亲和力可以通过添加胆汁得到补偿。尽管胆汁增强了HBGA结合,但它却降低了对GII.12的血清和单克隆抗体中和能力。这些观察结果表明,胆汁介导的病毒衣壳构象可塑性对配体识别和某些GII基因型的潜在免疫逃逸具有平衡影响。对于GII.2 HuNoV,胆汁具有类似的效果,但对GII.6或GII.4 HuNoV的HBGA结合和血清-配体阻断能力没有影响,这表明GII HuNoV菌株可能利用多种机制来确保对组胺血型抗原的广泛结合和抗原多样性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)是急性胃肠炎的主要病因之一,年轻儿童和老年人承担着最大的疾病负担。本研究旨在了解衣壳变异和胆汁如何影响GII.12 HuNoV对组胺血型抗原(HBGA)的识别和血清中和能力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究表征了两种同时共循环的GII.12 暴发菌株,它们在五个关键VP1位点上存在差异。这些菌株被用于模拟遗传变化对病毒衣壳配体和抗体结合的影响。研究重点在于GII.12 HuNoV菌株及其与组胺血型抗原配体和免疫识别的相互作用。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用突变分析评估VP1位点373和392的氨基酸变化对HBGA配体结合的影响。血清学分析评估了这些变化的抗原性影响。更广泛的GII比较分析了胆汁对HBGA结合和中和抗体效力的可变影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: 突变分析表明,VP1位点373和392的氨基酸共同调控HBGA配体结合。血清学分析显示这些位点的抗原性影响较小。更广泛的GII比较揭示了胆汁影响的差异,胆汁增强了GII.2和GII.12对HBGA的结合,但对GII.4和GII.6则没有这种效果。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,胆汁介导的病毒衣壳构象可塑性可以调节某些GII基因型的配体识别和免疫逃逸。本研究为GII.12 HuNoV菌株的持续传播提供了潜在的机制证据。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些数据有助于理解特定GII HuNoV菌株如何调节与组胺血型抗原配体和免疫识别相关的衣壳残基,这可能对针对GII.12菌株的抗病毒药物、疫苗和治疗方案的开发具有重要意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于仅聚焦于两种GII.12菌株,这可能无法代表GII.12 HuNoV的全部遗传多样性。证据强度中等,因为它是基于有限菌株的突变和血清学分析。

title: Occurrence of Norovirus and Hepatitis A Virus RNA in Agricultural Soil from Produce Farms in Ohio and Georgia
abstract: Although foodborne viruses are considered ubiquitous in the environment, studies on their presence in soil are largely lacking. In this field study, 168 agricultural soil samples were collected from farms in Georgia and Ohio over seven and eight months, respectively. A total RNA isolation method was developed, and extracted genetic material was analyzed using reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) to detect human norovirus and hepatitis A virus (HAV) RNA. Nearly 6% of samples (n = 10) tested positive for HAV RNA, while norovirus genogroup I and II were detected in 1.2% (n = 2) and 0.6% (n = 1) of samples, respectively. Despite samples being stored at −20 °C for an average of two years prior to testing, viruses remained detectable, although in low levels. CrAssphage DNA and pepper mild mottle virus (PMMoV) RNA were assessed as indicators of human fecal contamination in positive samples; however, neither was detected, precluding any correlation with the viral pathogens—likely due to differing characteristics between the indicators and target viruses. These findings provide valuable insight into the prevalence and diversity of foodborne viruses in agricultural soil and highlight its potential as a vehicle for virus transport to other matrices within a fresh produce farm environment.

abstract_zh: 尽管食源性病毒被认为普遍存在于环境中,但针对其在土壤中分布情况的研究仍较为缺乏。在这项实地研究中,分别历时7个月和8个月,从佐治亚州和俄亥俄州的农场采集了168份农业土壤样本。研究人员建立了一种总RNA分离方法,并采用逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)分析提取的遗传物质,以检测人诺如病毒和甲型肝炎病毒(HAV)RNA。近6%的样本(n = 10)HAV RNA检测呈阳性,而样本中诺如病毒基因组I和II的检出率分别为1.2%(n = 2)和0.6%(n = 1)。尽管样本在检测前平均于−20 °C条件下储存了2年,病毒仍可检出,但检出水平较低。研究在阳性样本中评估了CrAssphage DNA和辣椒轻斑驳病毒(PMMoV)RNA作为人粪便污染指标的情况;然而,两者均未检出,因此无法与病毒性病原体进行相关性分析,这可能是由于指标物与目标病毒的特性不同所致。这些发现为深入了解患病率以及食源性病毒的多样性提供了宝贵认识,并凸显了其在新鲜农产品农场环境中作为病毒向其他基质转移媒介的潜在作用。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查农业土壤中诺如病毒和戊型肝炎病毒RNA的分布,以解决关于食源性病毒在这些环境中的研究不足问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在俄亥俄州和佐治亚州分别历时七个月和八个月进行,从农产品农场收集了168份农业土壤样本。
analysis_zh.methods: 从土壤样本中提取总RNA,并使用逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)检测人类诺如病毒和戊型肝炎病毒(HAV)RNA。
analysis_zh.main_results: 检测到HAV RNA的样本占近6%(n = 10),而诺如病毒基因组I和II分别在1.2%(n = 2)和0.6%(n = 1)的样本中被发现。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,土壤中这些病毒的存在表明其在新鲜农产品农场环境中的潜在运输作用,强调了进一步研究的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了监测农业土壤中食源性病毒的重要性,以更好地了解其在污染新鲜农产品和增加公共卫生风险中的作用。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究证据受到样本储存条件可能导致的假阴性结果的限制,结果基于单一检测方法,可能无法捕捉到所有病毒变体。

title: Enteric pathogens associated with diarrhea in children under five years of age in Yogyakarta, Indonesia (2017–2018): a hospital-based surveillance study
abstract: Diarrhea is a major public health problem globally and remains an important cause of death and malnutrition in children under five years of age. In Indonesia, the burden of pediatric diarrhea remains substantial, yet most previous etiologic studies have focused on single pathogens, limiting understanding of the broader spectrum of enteric coinfections. This study aimed to identify the causes of diarrhea in hospitalized children under five years of age in Indonesia. Children aged < 5 years who were admitted to two participating hospitals in Yogyakarta with a diagnosis of diarrhea were prospectively recruited through active diarrhea surveillance between 2017 and 2018. Stool samples were collected during the first 48 h of admission and stored at -20 °C. Of 325 enrolled children, 171 stool samples (53%; 79 in 2017 and 92 in 2018) were randomly selected from eligible cases (acute, persistent, watery, or bloody diarrhea) by quarter, based on sufficient specimen availability. Multipathogen detection was performed using TaqMan Array Cards (TACs) at the Wellcome Trust Research Laboratory, Vellore, India. Targets with a cycle threshold (Ct) value < 40 were considered positive. Of the 325 hospitalized children, 171 (53%) underwent TAC testing (79 in 2017 and 92 in 2018). Rotavirus was the most frequently detected enteropathogen, accounting for 39% of TAC-tested samples in 2017 and 37% in 2018. Other commonly detected pathogens included adenovirus 40/41 (28% in 2017 and 3% in 2018), enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) (27% and 28%, respectively), and norovirus GII (11% and 10%, respectively). The majority of rotavirus-positive samples had at least one additional pathogen detected (81% in 2017 and 74% in 2018), with bacterial pathogens being the most common coinfecting agents. Multiple pathogens detected in the same sample were recorded individually; however, co-infections were not analyzed as a separate category. Therefore, the potential contribution of co-infection to disease severity could not be fully assessed and should be considered a limitation of the study. title: Pseudovirus Nanoparticles Displaying the Receptor-Binding Glycoprotein of Marburg Virus as Potential Vaccine Candidates
abstract: Background: The lack of a licensed vaccine against the deadly Marburg virus (MARV) calls for the development of a novel and effective vaccine strategy. Methods: We report here our development of three pseudovirus nanoparticles (PVNPs), each displaying a MARV-neutralizing glycoprotein (GP) segment of different lengths, as MARV vaccine candidates. These PVNPs, designated S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, were generated using our proprietary norovirus shell nanoparticle (SNP) platform. The PVNPs were evaluated for their production, self-assembly, morphology, structural properties, and immunogenicity. Results: Our data demonstrated that the three recombinant S-GP proteins, S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, can be produced at low cost using an E. coli expression system. The purified recombinant S-GP proteins self-assembled into PVNPs with high efficacy. Structural modeling of the S-GP1 PVNPs highlighted their key architectural features, consisting of an icosahedral inner shell and multiple trimeric GP structures displayed on the surface. Immunization of mice with the S-GP PVNPs elicited high titers of GP-specific antibodies, including IgG and IgA. Conclusions: Collectively, these data support the notion that the S-GP PVNPs may serve as potential MARV vaccine candidates worthy of further development.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a novel vaccine strategy against the deadly Marburg virus (MARV) by creating pseudovirus nanoparticles (PVNPs) that display segments of the MARV-neutralizing glycoprotein (GP). The PVNPs, generated using a proprietary norovirus shell nanoparticle (SNP) platform, were evaluated for production, self-assembly, morphology, structural properties, and immunogenicity. Results showed that the recombinant S-GP proteins could be produced at low cost using an E. coli expression system and self-assembled into PVNPs with high efficacy. Structural modeling revealed an icosahedral inner shell and multiple trimeric GP structures on the surface. Immunization of mice with the PVNPs elicited high titers of GP-specific antibodies, including IgG and IgA. The authors concluded that these PVNPs may serve as potential MARV vaccine candidates for further development. The study provides a foundation for exploring new vaccine platforms against MARV, which could have significant implications for public health and the prevention of viral hemorrhagic fevers. However, the evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for the study.

title: Etiological Profile, Clinical Characteristics, and Mean Platelet Volume in Children with Acute Gastroenteritis: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Aim: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) remains a common cause of pediatric morbidity and healthcare use. This study evaluated etiological agents, clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, complications, and the potential role of mean platelet volume (MPV) in children with AGE.Material and Method: In this retrospective study, 630 children aged 0-17 years who were diagnosed with AGE between January 2013 and December 2019 at a tertiary university hospital were reviewed. Only patients with a confirmed etiological diagnosis and no chronic systemic disease were included. Demographic data, clinical findings, laboratory parameters, stool analyses, treatment characteristics, and complications were analyzed according to etiological groups.Results: Rotavirus was the most frequently identified pathogen (27.5%), followed by Entamoeba histolytica (24.6%), rotavirusadenovirus co-infection (21.3%), adenovirus (10.6%), Giardia intestinalis (8.4%), and Clostridioides difficile (7.6%). Cases were most frequent in winter (46.4%). Viral agents predominated in younger children, whereas parasitic infections were more common in older age groups. No complications occurred in 77.0% of patients; seizures (10.8%), intussusception (5.1%), hemolytic uremic syndrome (3.0%), and renal failure (1.7%) were recorded. MPV differed significantly between etiological groups, with the highest values observed in rotavirusadenovirus co-infections and the lowest values in adenovirusrelated AGE (p=0.018). CRP values did not differ significantly among etiological groups.Conclusion: Rotavirus remained the most common etiological agent of pediatric acute gastroenteritis in this cohort. Although MPV values differed significantly among etiological groups, the observed differences were modest and do not support the use of MPV as an independent diagnostic marker. Nevertheless, MPV may serve as a supportive laboratory parameter when interpreted together with clinical and microbiological findings. Accurate etiological diagnosis remains essential for guiding appropriate treatment decisions and avoiding unnecessary antibiotic use in children with acute gastroenteritis. Further prospective multicenter studies are required to clarify its diagnostic and prognostic value in pediatric acute gastroenteritis.

title: Introduction
abstract: Abstract Background Diarrhoea remains a major cause of death in children under five, despite the global decline in hospitalisations following the widespread introduction of rotavirus vaccines . As rotavirus-associated disease declines, it is important to identify other diarrhoea associated pathogens, although post-vaccine data remain limited in Mozambique. This study aimed to estimate the incidence and determine the aetiology of Moderate-to-Severe Diarrhoea (MSD) and Less Severe Diarrhoea (LSD) among children under five, post-rotavirus vaccine introduction in Manhiça District, a rural setting in Mozambique. Methods We estimated the incidence of diarrhoea using data from the morbidity surveillance and pathogen-attributable fractions based on analysis of stool specimens collected in a case–control study. Results The overall incidence of MSD was 5.6 cases per 1,000 child-years at risk (CYAR), with the highest rate observed among infants aged 0–11 months (15.5 per 1,000 CYAR) with a declining trend over time. LSD incidence was approximately 20 times higher than MSD incidence (119.7 per 1,000 CYAR), peaking among children aged 12–23 months (232.9 per 1,000 CYAR). Rotavirus remained the leading cause of both MSD and LSD among infants aged 0–11 months, while other important pathogens associated with LSD in this age group included sapovirus and Cryptosporidium spp. Among children aged 12–23 months, enteroaggregative Escherichia coli and adenovirus 40/41 were the major contributors to MSD. Conclusions Our findings highlight that rotavirus remains an important diarrhoea aetiology among infants and demonstrate changes on diarrhoea aetiologies post-rotavirus vaccine introduction; reinforcing the need for continued surveillance to better inform control and prevention strategies.

source_records.title: Incidence and aetiology of diarrhoeal disease among children under five years in the post-rotavirus vaccine introduction era in Manhiça District, Mozambique
source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Diarrhoea remains a major cause of death in children under five, despite the global decline in hospitalisations following the widespread introduction of rotavirus vaccines . As rotavirus-associated disease declines, it is important to identify other diarrhoea associated pathogens, although post-vaccine data remain limited in Mozambique. This study aimed to estimate the incidence and determine the aetiology of Moderate-to-Severe Diarrhoea (MSD) and Less Severe Diarrhoea (LSD) among children under five, post-rotavirus vaccine introduction in Manhiça District, a rural setting in Mozambique. Methods We estimated the incidence of diarrhoea using data from the morbidity surveillance and pathogen-attributable fractions based on analysis of stool specimens collected in a case–control study. Results The overall incidence of MSD was 5.6 cases per 1,000 child-years at risk (CYAR), with the highest rate observed among infants aged 0–11 months (15.5 per 1,000 CYAR) with a declining trend over time. LSD incidence was approximately 20 times higher than MSD incidence (119.7 per 1,000 CYAR), peaking among children aged 12–23 months (232.9 per 1,000 CYAR). Rotavirus remained the leading cause of both MSD and LSD among infants aged 0–11 months, while other important pathogens associated with LSD in this age group included sapovirus and Cryptosporidium spp. Among children aged 12–23 months, enteroaggregative Escherichia coli and adenovirus 40/41 were the major contributors to MSD. Conclusions Our findings highlight that rotavirus remains an important diarrhoea aetiology among infants and demonstrate changes on diarrhoea aetiologies post-rotavirus vaccine introduction; reinforcing the need for continued surveillance to better inform control and prevention strategies.

title: Deep untargeted wastewater metagenomic sequencing from sewersheds across the United States
abstract: Wastewater monitoring enables non-invasive, population-scale tracking of community infections independent of healthcare-seeking behavior and clinical diagnosis. Metagenomic sequencing extends this capability by enabling broad, pathogen-agnostic detection of hundreds of viral taxa, including emerging threats. Here, we present data from CASPER (the Coalition for Agnostic Sequencing of Pathogens from Environmental Reservoirs), a U.S.-based wastewater metagenomic sequencing network designed for deep, untargeted pathogen monitoring at national scale. This release includes 1,206 samples collected between December 2023 and December 2025 from 27 sites across nine states, covering 13 million people. Deep sequencing (~1 billion read pairs per sample) generated 1.2 trillion read pairs (358 terabases), capturing diverse human, animal, and plant viruses including rare taxa. CASPER data tracks wastewater digital PCR and clinical abundance trends for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and respiratory syncytial virus, and recovers national-scale variant dynamics for SARS-CoV-2 and norovirus. As the largest publicly available untargeted wastewater sequencing dataset to date, CASPER provides a shared and growing resource for pathogen surveillance and microbial ecology.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents the CASPER dataset, a large-scale wastewater metagenomic sequencing project designed to monitor human noroviruses across the United States. The research aimed to address the need for non-invasive, population-level tracking of community infections, independent of clinical diagnosis. Using deep sequencing, the study captured diverse viral taxa, including rare human norovirus variants, and provided insights into their abundance and dynamics. The findings highlight the potential of wastewater sequencing for surveillance and microbial ecology research, offering a novel approach for tracking norovirus infections. The dataset includes 1,206 samples from 27 sites across nine states, covering 13 million people, and is the largest publicly available untargeted wastewater sequencing resource. While the study is limited by its reliance on wastewater samples, it provides a valuable tool for understanding norovirus transmission and prevalence.

full_text: Abstract Background Norovirus (NoV) is a major pathogen responsible for acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. Children, due to their underdeveloped immune systems and higher risk of exposure, constitute a population with a relatively concentrated incidence of infection and disease burden. In recent years, research on NoV infections in children has been growing globally; however, there remains a lack of systematic quantitative analysis regarding the evolution of research themes, models of international collaboration, and future development directions in this field. Therefore, this study employs bibliometric methods to conduct a visual analysis of the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and development trends in the global field of NoV infection research in children, providing a reference for future scientific research and the formulation of prevention and control strategies. Methods This study retrieved literature on pediatric NoV infections published between January 1998 and December 2025 from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software, we conducted a visual analysis of annual publication trends, countries/regions, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and references to reveal the research trajectory, knowledge base, and cutting-edge directions in this field. Results This study included a total of 2,161 relevant publications. The results show that research on NoV infections in children worldwide has generally followed a steady upward trend, with activity remaining high in recent years. The United States, China, and Japan are the leading contributors to research in this field, with the United States exerting significant influence through international collaboration. The University of Tokyo, Emory University, and Chiang Mai University are the research institutions with the highest number of publications. Vinje, Jan; Ushijima, Hiroshi; and Khamrin, Pattara were the most prolific core authors, while Atmar, Robert L.; Lindesmith, Lisa C.; and Patel, Manish M. demonstrated strong academic influence. Keyword analysis revealed that research in this field primarily focuses on viral molecular characteristics, epidemiological features, and clinical manifestations in children, and is gradually expanding toward disease burden assessment, global prevention and control strategies, and vaccine development. Conclusion Global research on NoV infections in children has evolved into a Multi-Disciplinary research framework driven by virology, epidemiology, clinical medicine, and public health. Current research focuses primarily on molecular epidemiology and genetic diversity, as well as epidemiological characteristics and outbreak transmission mechanisms, while the assessment of disease burden and the optimization of global prevention and control strategies are gradually emerging as key future research directions. In the future, international collaboration, multicenter surveillance, and interdisciplinary research should be further strengthened to advance research on pediatric NoV infection from describing disease characteristics toward precision surveillance, proactive prevention, and comprehensive control and prevention measures. Introduction Norovirus (NoV) is one of the primary pathogens causing acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. It is highly contagious and spreads rapidly, is prevalent worldwide, and is considered the fifth leading cause of disability-adjusted life years in the global disease burden [1]. The general population is widely susceptible to NoV, with over 700 million cases of infection and 200,000 deaths reported annually. Children under 5 years of age have the highest incidence rate, and this age group also has the highest diarrhea-related mortality rate [2, 3]. NoV is primarily transmitted via the fecal–oral route, accounting for 63.20% of foodborne viral infections. It can spread rapidly through contaminated shellfish, fruits, vegetables, ready-to-eat foods, and water sources, and is prone to causing cluster outbreaks in areas with poor sanitation in developing countries. Currently, there are no specific antiviral drugs or vaccines available [4]. In recent years, the number of NoV infections and outbreaks worldwide has continued to rise, causing serious impacts on human health and economic development [5]. Research findings on NoV infections in children continue to expand, with studies characterized by significant differences in research directions, scattered evidence, and intersecting disciplinary contexts. Traditional narrative reviews rely heavily on individual researchers’ literature screening and subjective interpretations, making it difficult to objectively quantify changes in publication timing within the field, connections among international research collaborations, and the evolution of knowledge. Meta-analyses can only conduct pooled effect analyses on a specific type of homogeneous clinical trial data to address specific scientific questions; they cannot trace shifts in research hotspots from a holistic perspective or identify seminal foundational literature and emerging research directions. In contrast, bibliometrics, drawing on mathematical statistics, information metrics, and visualization algorithms, enables unbiased quantitative analysis of large-scale literature datasets. It intuitively presents macro-level information such as annual output patterns, transnational collaboration networks, core research platforms, and the evolution of thematic clusters, thereby accurately identifying developmental blind spots and future frontier directions in the field [6]. Given the current heavy global burden of NoV infection among children and the persistent challenges in prevention and control, there is an urgent need to systematically map out the complete knowledge landscape of this field from a macro-level. Therefore, introducing bibliometric methods to conduct a panoramic quantitative analysis holds significant theoretical reference value and practical guidance. Through our preliminary search of major global academic databases, we found that there is still a gap in bibliometric research on NoV infection in children. Based on this, this study compiled basic information on global research related to NoV infection in children from 1998 to 2025. By using Citespace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software to construct knowledge maps of the papers, the study aims to explore the current state of global research in this field, identify research hotspots, and outline future trends, thereby providing valuable direction and reference for future scientific exploration. Materials and methods Data sources and search strategies Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) is a Multi-Disciplinary citation index database developed by Clarivate Analytics. It includes more than 20,000 authoritative journals that have undergone rigorous peer review, covering over 250 disciplines. It features comprehensive metadata on authors, institutions, keywords, and references, preserves complete citation links, and allows for the direct batch export of standardized data compatible with bibliometric software. It is widely recognized as the most authoritative benchmark data source for constructing knowledge graphs [7, 8]. Although PubMed has advantages in biomedical retrieval, it lacks a complete structured citation index and cannot support core network analyses such as co-citation and literature coupling; Scopus has lower journal inclusion thresholds, incomplete retroactive citation tracking for early publications, and poor compatibility of its metadata format with mainstream bibliometric tools, which can easily introduce manual correction biases; Google Scholar contains a large amount of low-quality gray literature, resulting in distorted citation counts, and lacks standardized batch export functionality, making it difficult to meet the requirements for quantitative graph analysis [9, 10]. Therefore, this study selected WoSCC as the sole data source to ensure the accuracy and authority of the analysis results. On 1 April 2026, we searched the WoSCC (SCI-Expanded) database using the following search formula: TS = ((“Norovirus” OR “Norwalk virus” OR “Human noroviruses”) AND (“children” OR “infantile” OR “child” OR ‘childhood’ OR “pediatric”)). The search date range was set from 1 January 1998 to 31 December 2025; only articles and reviews were retained, and the language was restricted to “English”. Two researchers conducted the search and extracted data simultaneously and independently, with a third researcher performing the final verification to avoid selective bias. After collation, a total of 2,161 articles were ultimately included; all publications were exported as.txt files in “full record and reference list” format. The detailed search process is shown in Fig. 1. Bibliometric analysis CiteSpace is a bibliometric and scientific knowledge graph visualization tool developed by Professor Chen Chaomei’s team at Drexel University in the United States. It runs on Java and integrates citation analysis, complex network algorithms, temporal change detection, and information visualization technologies [11]. It is specifically designed to uncover the underlying patterns of association and evolutionary trajectories within long-term bibliographic datasets. We used CiteSpace (6.4.R1 Advanced) to visualize journal emergence, keyword clustering, keyword emergence, and reference emergence. Parameter settings: The “Time Slicing” range was set to 1998–2025, “Years Per Slice” was set to “1”, and “Node Types” were selected as “Journals”, “Keywords”, and “References”, respectively. For “Selection Criteria”, the default “g-index” (coefficient K = 25) was used. VOSviewer is a free, open-source bibliometric visualization tool developed by the Center for Science and Technology Studies at Leiden University in the Netherlands. It offers three interactive visualization modes: network view, overlay view, and density view [12]. We used VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) to analyze network patterns across countries, institutions, journals, authors, keywords, and references. For 'Type of analysis', 'Co-authorship' was selected for authors, institutions, and countries, while 'Co-occurrence' was selected for keywords and references. The 'Counting method' was set to 'Full counting', and the minimum item threshold was set to 2 occurrences. Display parameters and 'Labels' sizes were adjusted to reduce overlap and improve readability. Finally, 'Overlay Visualization' and 'Density Visualization' were selected for visual analysis. Bibliometrix is a comprehensive scientific mapping analysis system based on the R language that covers data import, cleaning, quantitative statistics, network analysis, and chart output [13]. In this study, we used it to visualize country collaborations and keyword frequencies. Prior to network analysis, country/region names were standardized using a predefined thesaurus. Three sovereign states—China, the United Kingdom, and the USA—had multiple alternative labels in the WoSCC export (including constituent countries, special administrative regions, and overseas territories); all such variants were merged under a single standardized label for each state. This merging rule was applied consistently across the dataset. A complete mapping of all original WoSCC country/region strings to standardized labels is provided in Supplementary File S1. Quality control Quality control was conducted in accordance with the preliminary BIBLIO guidelines [14], with six methodological items explicitly operationalized: data sources (Item 6), search strategy (Item 7), eligibility criteria (Item 9), data refinement (Item 10), quality assessment (Item 11), and data synthesis (Item 12). During literature retrieval and eligibility screening, two reviewers independently assessed all records, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer; inter-rater reliability was excellent (Cohen's κ = 0.92), as further detailed in Sect. "Data sources and search strategies". Country/region entity standardization and all software parameter thresholds were predefined prior to analysis, as described in Sect. "Bibliometric analysis". To support reproducibility, three supplementary files are provided: the per-record screening log (Supplementary File S2), the complete country/region thesaurus (Supplementary File S1), and a completed BIBLIO checklist mapping all 20 items to their corresponding locations in the manuscript (Supplementary File S3). These quality-control measures were applied uniformly throughout the study to mitigate selection bias and ensure methodological transparency. Results Trends in the number of publications Overall, the annual number of publications in this field has shown a clear upward trend over the past 28 years, although the rate of growth has varied somewhat across different periods (Fig. 2). From 1998 to 2004, the field was in its early stages, with an overall low annual output that fluctuated slightly, increasing from 6 papers in 1998 to 24 in 2004. From 2005 to 2013, research entered a phase of steady growth, with annual output gradually rising from 33 to 83 papers, indicating that NoV infection in children was gradually attracting more attention from researchers. From 2014 to 2025, research activity in this field increased significantly, with the annual number of publications exceeding 100 for the first time, reaching 122. It has since remained at a relatively high level overall, peaking at 150 in 2021—the highest figure during the study period. Between 2022 and 2025, the annual number of publications fluctuated somewhat but remained above 100. At the same time, the overall trend in annual citations generally followed the trend in publication volume, with citations exceeding 5,000 in each of the past five years. Overall, annual publications increased from 6 in 1998 to a peak of 150 in 2021, and annual citations exceeded 5,000 in each of the past five years, reflecting a sustained upward trend in research output and attention over the study period. Analysis of countries/regions and institutions A total of 130 countries/regions and 2,882 research institutions worldwide participated in studies related to NoV infection in children. The top three countries/regions in terms of publication volume were, in order, the USA (406 papers), CHINA (307 papers), and JAPAN (193 papers); together, these three contributed more than 40% of the research output and represent the most significant sources of research in this field (Table 1). The composition of single-country and multinational collaborative publications is shown in Fig. 3A. A comparison of MCP values reveals that the USA not only leads in total publications but also ranks first globally in the number of multinational collaborative publications; Japan has a relatively high proportion of international collaborative publications; and China, although second in total publications, has a relatively low proportion of multinational collaborative publications. In Fig. 3B, the lines connecting nodes represent co-authorship relationships between two countries/regions in the same publication; line thickness is positively correlated with collaboration frequency. The USA exhibits dense co-authorship links with multiple countries in Europe, Oceania, South America, and Asia, demonstrating the widest scope of collaboration; China and Japan also have multiple co-authorship links with neighboring Asian countries as well as European and American nations, indicating a high level of Participation. The overall network exhibits a cross-regional interconnected structure, with no completely isolated national nodes; direct or indirect co-occurrence collaboration links exist among the three major research regions of North America, East Asia, and Europe. The USA, Australia, and Germany rank among the top in terms of citations per paper, indicating that their research findings receive greater overall attention (Table 1). The top three institutions by publication volume are The University of Tokyo (84 papers), Emory University (66 papers), and Chiang Mai University (62 papers). The remaining high-output institutions are primarily U.S. universities and specialized research institutes, with Baylor College of Medicine receiving the highest number of citations among these high-output institutions (Table 2). The co-occurrence network of institutions within the field (Fig. 3C) can be divided into seven clusters. High-output institutions such as The University of Tokyo, Emory University, and Chiang Mai University serve as the core nodes of their respective clusters, possessing the highest number of co-occurrence connections within their clusters. In Fig. 3D, institutions with a greenish hue—represented by The University of Tokyo—have long been deeply engaged in the field of pediatric NoV infection and serve as the foundational forces supporting the field’s development; larger yellow nodes, such as Emory University, gained momentum rapidly during the middle and later stages of research, becoming the backbone of the field with the highest levels of research output and collaboration activity in recent years. Smaller bright yellow nodes, such as Chang Gung University and the Evandro Chagas Institute, represent emerging research forces that have gradually joined the global collaboration network in recent years. The overall institutional collaboration network has continued to expand over time, forming an evolutionary pattern characterized by the joint development of multiple tiers. Analysis of authors and cited authors A total of 1,049 researchers contributed to studies on NoV infection in children. The three most productive authors were Jan Vinje (81 publications), Hiroshi Ushijima (80), and Pattara Khamrin (59), with other highly productive authors mainly from Japan and the United States (Table 3). abstract_original: Therefore, this study employs bibliometric methods to conduct a visual analysis of the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and development trends in the global field of NoV infection research in children, providing a reference for future scientific research and the formulation of prevention and control strategies. Methods This study retrieved literature on pediatric NoV infections published between January 1998 and December 2025 from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software, we conducted a visual analysis of annual publication trends, countries/regions, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and references to reveal the research trajectory, knowledge base, and cutting-edge directions in this field. Results This study included a total of 2,161 relevant publications. The results show that research on NoV infections in children worldwide has generally followed a steady upward trend, with activity remaining high in recent years. Conclusion Global research on NoV infections in children has evolved into a Multi-Disciplinary research framework driven by virology, epidemiology, clinical medicine, and public health. Abstract Background Norovirus (NoV) is a major pathogen responsible for acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. Children, due to their underdeveloped immune systems and higher risk of exposure, constitute a population with a relatively concentrated incidence of infection and disease burden. In recent years, research on NoV infections in children has been growing globally; however, there remains a lack of systematic quantitative analysis regarding the evolution of research themes, models of international collaboration, and future development directions in this field. abstract_zh: 因此,本研究采用文献计量方法,对全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究领域的知识结构、研究热点和发展趋势进行可视化分析,为未来科学研究和防控策略的制定提供参考。方法 本研究从Web of Science核心合集(WoSCC)数据库中检索了1998年1月至2025年12月期间发表的关于儿童诺如病毒感染的文献。使用CiteSpace、VOSviewer和Bibliometrix软件,对年度发表趋势、国家/地区、机构、作者、期刊、关键词和参考文献进行了可视化分析,以揭示该领域的研究轨迹、知识基础和前沿方向。结果 本研究共纳入2,161篇相关文献。结果显示,全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究总体呈稳步上升趋势,近年来研究活动依然保持较高水平。结论 全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究已发展为由病毒学、诺如病毒、临床医学和公共卫生驱动的多学科研究框架。摘要 背景 诺如病毒(NoV)是人类急性胃肠炎和腹泻的主要病原体。由于儿童免疫系统尚未发育成熟且暴露风险较高,其感染和疾病负担相对集中。近年来,全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究不断增长;然而,该领域仍缺乏关于研究主题的系统定量分析、国际合作模式以及未来发展方向的深入探讨。该病毒具有高度传染性,传播迅速,全球广泛流行,被认为是全球疾病负担中导致失能调整生命年(DALYs)损失的第五大原因[1]。

title: Systematic functional, genomic, and safety evaluation of food-derived anti-human norovirus candidate Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001
abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 is a yogurt-derived strain previously reported to bind GII.4 human norovirus (HuNoV) and inhibit viral replication in zebrafish larvae. Here, its in vitro probiotic properties and preliminary safety were evaluated together with whole-genome analysis. The 2.87-Mb genome (46.67% GC; 2757 coding sequences) shared 97.66% average nucleotide identity with L. rhamnosus GG ATCC 53103. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed acid and bile tolerance, retaining approximately 30% survival after 3 h at pH 2.0 and over 40% after 4 h in 0.2% bile salts. During sequential simulated gastrointestinal digestion, L. rhamnosus YQ001 retained 35.98% survival after the gastric phase and 45.06% after the intestinal phase. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed over 90% auto-aggregation at 24 h, while its cell-free supernatant exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities of 85.17% and 76.35%, respectively. Antibacterial activity detected by agar diffusion was abolished after pH neutralization, indicating that the observed inhibition was largely pH-dependent under the tested conditions. L. rhamnosus YQ001 was non-hemolytic and negative for gelatinase and nitroreductase activities. Overall, the phenotypic and genomic findings support the probiotic potential of L. rhamnosus YQ001, while further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is warranted.

The findings suggest potential probiotic use for norovirus infection, though further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is required. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估一种从酸奶中分离的乳酸乳球菌YZQ001的益生菌特性和安全性,该菌株此前报道可结合GII.4人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)并在斑马鱼幼鱼中抑制病毒复制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了乳酸乳球菌YZQ001的体外益生菌特性和初步安全性,以及其全基因组分析,未指定特定的研究设计或人群。
elements_zh.methods: 通过体外试验评估了乳酸乳球菌YZQ001的益生菌特性,包括酸和胆盐耐受性、自聚集能力和自由基清除能力。进行了全基因组分析以比较其与其他菌株的遗传特征。
elements_zh.main_results: 乳酸乳球菌YZQ001表现出酸和胆盐耐受性,在pH 2.0条件下3小时后存活率约为30%,在0.2%胆盐中4小时后存活率超过40%。在连续模拟胃肠消化过程中,其在胃部消化阶段后存活率为35.98%,在肠道消化阶段后存活率为45.06%。该菌株在24小时后表现出超过90%的自聚集能力,并分别表现出85.17%和76.35%的DPPH和ABTS自由基清除能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 表型和基因组研究结果表明,乳酸乳球菌YZQ001具有作为益生菌的潜力,尽管需要进一步进行菌株特异性功能和安全性评估。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为诺如病毒感染的益生菌候选菌株的使用提供了初步支持,可能对未来该领域的研究和开发提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外评估,未包括临床或体内测试,这可能影响研究结果的普遍适用性。由于缺乏全面的安全性和有效性数据,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 乳酸乳球菌YZQ001是一种从酸奶中分离的菌株,此前报道可结合GII.4人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)并在斑马鱼幼鱼中抑制病毒复制。本研究对其体外益生菌特性及初步安全性进行了评估,并进行了全基因组分析。该菌株的全基因组为2.87 Mb(GC含量46.67%;包含2757个编码序列),与乳酸乳球菌GG ATCC 53103的平均核苷酸同源性为97.66%。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001表现出酸和胆盐耐受性,在pH 2.0条件下3小时后存活率约为30%,在0.2%胆盐中4小时后存活率超过40%。在连续模拟胃肠消化过程中,乳酸乳球菌YZQ001在胃部消化阶段后存活率为35.98%,在肠道消化阶段后存活率为45.06%。该菌株在24小时后表现出超过90%的自聚集能力,其无细胞培养上清液表现出85.17%的DPPH自由基清除能力和76.35%的ABTS自由基清除能力。通过琼脂扩散法检测到的抗菌活性在pH中和后被消除,表明在测试条件下观察到的抑制作用主要依赖于pH值。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001不溶血,且不表现出明胶酶和硝基还原酶活性。总体而言,表型和基因组研究结果支持乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为益生菌的潜力,但需要进一步进行菌株特异性功能和安全性评估。
summary_zh: 乳酸乳球菌YZQ001是一种从酸奶中分离的菌株,此前报道可结合GII.4人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)并在斑马鱼幼鱼中抑制病毒复制。本研究对其体外益生菌特性及初步安全性进行了评估,并进行了全基因组分析。该菌株的全基因组为2.87 Mb(GC含量46.67%;包含2757个编码序列),与乳酸乳球菌GG ATCC 53103的平均核苷酸同源性为97.66%。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001表现出酸和胆盐耐受性,在pH 2.0条件下3小时后存活率约为30%,在0.2%胆盐中4小时后存活率超过40%。在连续模拟胃肠消化过程中,乳酸乳球菌YZQ001在胃部消化阶段后存活率为35.98%,在肠道消化阶段后存活率为45.06%。该菌株在24小时后表现出超过90%的自聚集能力,其无细胞培养上清液表现出85.17%的DPPH自由基清除能力和76.35%的ABTS自由基清除能力。通过琼脂扩散法检测到的抗菌活性在pH中和后被消除,表明在测试条件下观察到的抑制作用主要依赖于pH值。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001不溶血,且不表现出明胶酶和硝基还原酶活性。总体而言,表型和基因组研究结果支持乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为益生菌的潜力,但需要进一步进行菌株特异性功能和安全性评估。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估一种从酸奶中分离的乳酸乳球菌YZQ001的益生菌特性和安全性,该菌株此前报道可结合GII.4人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)并在斑马鱼幼鱼中抑制病毒复制。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了乳酸乳球菌YZQ001的体外益生菌特性和初步安全性,以及其全基因组分析,未指定特定的研究设计或人群。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过体外试验评估了乳酸乳球菌YZQ001的益生菌特性,包括酸和胆盐耐受性、自聚集能力和自由基清除能力。进行了全基因组分析以比较其与其他菌株的遗传特征。
analysis_zh.main_results: 乳酸乳球菌YZQ001表现出酸和胆盐耐受性,在pH 2.0条件下3小时后存活率约为30%,在0.2%胆盐中4小时后存活率超过40%。在连续模拟胃肠消化过程中,其在胃部消化阶段后存活率为35.98%,在肠道消化阶段后存活率为45.06%。该菌株在24小时后表现出超过90%的自聚集能力,并分别表现出85.17%和76.35%的DPPH和ABTS自由基清除能力。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 表型和基因组研究结果表明,乳酸乳球菌YZQ001具有作为益生菌的潜力,尽管需要进一步进行菌株特异性功能和安全性评估。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为诺如病毒感染的益生菌候选菌株的使用提供了初步支持,可能对未来该领域的研究和开发提供参考。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外评估,未包括临床或体内测试,这可能影响研究结果的普遍适用性。由于缺乏全面的安全性和有效性数据,证据强度中等。

title: Epidemiological insights into bovine viral diarrhea virus and bovine rotavirus in diarrheic Yaks on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau

source_records.title: Epidemiological insights into bovine viral diarrhea virus and bovine rotavirus in diarrheic Yaks on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
Epidemiological insights into bovine viral diarrhea virus and bovine rotavirus in diarrheic Yaks on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau

priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
full_text: AbstractDiarrhea is common in yak calves and causes substantial economic losses to the yak industry on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) and bovine rotavirus (BRV) are important enteric pathogens in cattle, but their epidemiology and potential association in yaks remain unclear. In this study, 1,623 fecal samples were collected from yaks across different locations, age groups, seasons, and breeds to investigate BVDV, BRV, and BVDV/BRV dual positivity. Viral positivity was detected using PCR amplification, and associated factors were analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariable binary logistic regression. Overall, 277 samples were positive for BVDV, 224 for BRV, and 92 for both viruses, corresponding to positivity rates of 17.07%, 13.80%, and 5.67%, respectively. BVDV positivity differed significantly among seasons (P = 0.0008), with a lower rate in summer than in spring and winter, and was strongly associated with BRV positivity (P < 0.0001). BRV positivity differed significantly by location, age, season, and breed in univariable analyses, and was higher in adult yaks than in calves (16.54% vs. 11.35%, P = 0.0025) but lower in summer than in spring and winter. Multivariable analysis showed that BRV status was the only factor associated with BVDV positivity (OR = 4.277, 95% CI: 3.121–5.861, P < 0.001), whereas age, sampling location, and BVDV status were associated with BRV positivity, with BVDV-positive yaks showing a markedly higher risk of BRV positivity (OR = 4.299, 95% CI: 3.138–5.889, P < 0.001). No factor was significantly associated with BVDV/BRV dual positivity. These findings indicate that BVDV and BRV circulate among yaks and are strongly associated, suggesting possible viral interaction or shared exposure conditions and highlighting the need for integrated surveillance and control strategies targeting multiple viral pathogens.Keywords: bovine rotavirus, bovine viral diarrhea virus, diarrhea, epidemiological investigation, Yak Materials and methodsExperimental designThis multiregional, cross-sectional survey aimed to investigate the epidemiological characteristics of BVDV and BRV infection in diarrheic yaks raised under a semi-grazing system in seven locations on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau between March 2024 and February 2025. The sampling sites included Nyingchi, Tibet Autonomous Region; Yushu Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province; Golog Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province; Derong County, Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province; Dege County, Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province; Daofu County, Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province; and Litang County, Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province (Figure 1). Fecal samples were collected from yaks exhibiting diarrhea-associated clinical signs, including watery or loose feces, dehydration, depression, and reduced appetite. Clinical status was assessed by local veterinarians or trained personnel at the time of sampling based on visible signs and information provided by herd owners. Only animals showing obvious diarrheic feces, with or without accompanying systemic signs, were included in this study. Relevant factors for each yak, including age, breed, sampling location, sampling season, and ambient temperature, was recorded for further analysis. Age was classified as adult (≥ 12 months) or calf (< 12 months). Breeds included Garzê–Aba–Jiulong yak (Jiulong), Tibetan alpine yak (Alpine), Qinghai Plateau yak (Plateau), and Garzê yak–cattle hybrid (Pien). Sampling locations included Nyingchi, Yushu, Golog, Derong, Dege, Daofu, and Litang. Sampling seasons were categorized as spring (March to May), summer (June to August), autumn (September to November), and winter (December to next year February). full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractDiarrhea is common in yak calves and causes substantial economic losses to the yak industry on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) and bovine rotavirus (BRV) are important enteric pathogens in cattle, but their epidemiology and potential association in yaks remain unclear. In this study, 1,623 fecal samples were collected from yaks across different locations, age groups, seasons, and breeds to investigate BVDV, BRV, and BVDV/BRV dual positivity. Viral positivity was detected using PCR amplification, and associated factors were analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariable binary logistic regression. Overall, 277 samples were positive for BVDV, 224 for BRV, and 92 for both viruses, corresponding to positivity rates of 17.07%, 13.80%, and 5.67%, respectively. BVDV positivity differed significantly among seasons (P = 0.0008), with a lower rate in summer than in spring and winter, and was strongly associated with BRV positivity (P < 0.0001). BRV positivity differed significantly by location, age, season, and breed in univariable analyses, and was higher in adult yaks than in calves (16.54% vs. 11.35%, P = 0.0025) but lower in summer than in spring and winter. Multivariable analysis showed that BRV status was the only factor associated with BVDV positivity (OR = 4.277, 95% CI: 3.121–5.861, P < 0.001), whereas age, sampling location, and BVDV status were associated with BRV positivity, with BVDV-positive yaks showing a markedly higher risk of BRV positivity (OR = 4.299, 95% CI: 3.138–5.889, P < 0.001). No factor was significantly associated with BVDV/BRV dual positivity. These findings indicate that BVDV and BRV circulate among yaks and are strongly associated, suggesting possible viral interaction or shared exposure conditions and highlighting the need for integrated surveillance and control strategies targeting multiple viral pathogens.Keywords: bovine rotavirus, bovine viral diarrhea virus, diarrhea, epidemiological investigation, Yak

full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionDiarrhea is one of the major challenges faced by yaks, severely affecting the development of the yak industry on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and causing substantial economic losses. For example, the prevalence of diarrhea prevalence in adult yaks and calves has been reported to be 12.22% and 20.91% respectively, with corresponding mortality rates if 15.71% and 28.29% (20). Although multiple pathogens, including intestinal parasites, Salmonella, Escherichia coli, BVDV, has been identified in diarrheic yaks (20), the contributions of BVDV and BRV to disease prevalence remain unclear, hindering vaccine development and the implementation of timely and effective prevention and control measures. Therefore, in the present study, the positivity of BVDV, BRV, and BVDV/BRV dual positivity in fecal samples collected from diarrheic yaks was systematically investigated and analyzed. Notably, because the samples were collected from multiple farms/herds through field-based convenience sampling, potential herd-level clustering could not be fully excluded. Therefore, the observed positivity rates should be interpreted as detection rates among submitted diarrheic yak samples rather than population-level prevalence estimates.BVDV and BRV infections may contribute to the prevalence of diarrhea in YaksViral pathogens, such as BVDV, BRV, bovine coronavirus (BCoV), bovine norovirus (BNoV), have been widely reported to be associated with diarrhea in domestic calves (20, 21). For example, in a case-control study investigating the microbiological etiology of calf diarrhea on cattle farms in the Midwestern United States, Cho et al. found that the positivity rate of BRV and BVDV in fecal samples from diarrheic calves were 27.1% and 0.5% (22). Recent epidemiological studies have also confirmed the circulation of BVDV and BRV in yaks (7, 19). Li et al, (23) reported that the overall antibody and antigen prevalences of BVDV in Qinghai Province from April 2024 to May 2025 were 84.52% (1,158/1,370) and 2.41% (33/1,370), respectively, indicating widespread previous exposure to BVDV and a relatively low proportion of animals with detectable antigenemia. In another study, Yan et al. (19) found that 73.6% of 541 diarrheic yak samples collected from 68 farms on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau between April 2015 to June 2018 were positive for BRV, suggesting that BRV is an important viral pathogen associated with yak diarrhea.In the present study, BVDV was detected in 17.07% (277/1,623) of fecal samples from diarrheic yaks (Figure 2B), which was markedly higher than the antigen prevalence reported by Li et al. (23), despite partial overlap in sampling period, sampling location, and sample size. This discrepancy may be explained by differences in the sampled populations and specimen types. First, our samples were collected specifically from diarrheic yaks, whereas Li et al. included yaks showing respiratory and/or diarrhea symptoms. Second, we detected BVDV nucleic acid in fecal samples, which may reflect intestinal viral shedding, whereas Li et al. antigen in serum, which more directly indicates systemic infection or antigenemia. Therefore, differences in clinical inclusion criteria and detection targets may have contributed to the higher BVDV positivity observed in our study. The BRV positivity rate in our study was 13.80% (224/1,623; Figure 3B), which was substantially lower than that reported by Yan et al (19). This difference may be attributable to variation in yak herds, sampling location, animal age composition, and diagnostic methods. Nevertheless, together with previous studies, our findings confirm that BVDV and BRV are widely circulating among yaks on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, suggesting that both viruses are involved in the pathogen spectrum of yak diarrhea and should be considered in etiological surveillance.Factors associated with BVDV and BRV positivity in YaksViral infections in cattle are influenced by multiple host-, pathogen-, environment-, and management-related factors, including age, season, geographic region, herd density, hygiene conditions, immune status, vaccination history, and the presence of persistently infected animals (21, 24, 25). For enteric viruses, age is among the most frequently reported risk factors. BRV infection is generally more common in neonatal calves, largely because young animals have immature immune systems and are dependent heavily on adequate passive transfer of maternal antibodies (21, 26). For example, Cho and Yoon summarized that BRV, BCoV, enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli, and Cryptosporidium parvum are major pathogens associated with neonatal calf diarrhea, with BRV infection occurring most frequently during the first weeks of life (21). Similarly, Cho et al. (22) reported that BRV was significantly associated with diarrhea in calves in the Midwestern United States, with a positivity rate of 27.1% in diarrheic calves, supporting the importance of age-related susceptibility in BRV-associated diarrhea. Season is another important factor affecting viral diarrhea. BRV is generally more stable under low-temperature and humid conditions, and outbreaks of calf diarrhea are often more frequent during cold seasons, when environmental viral survival is prolonged and host resistance may be weakened (27, 28). In addition, regional differences in climate, grazing pattern, herd structure, animal movement, and biosecurity practices can further influence viral transmission (7, 25, 29). For BVDV, herd-level factors are particularly important because persistently infected animals can continuously shed virus and maintain BVDV circulation within herds.In the present study, age, season, sampling location, and BVDV status were identified to be associated with BRV positivity in diarrheic yaks (Figure 3H). Notably, adult yaks showed a higher BRV positivity rate than calves (Figure 3D), which differs from most reports in domestic cattle, where BRV-associated diarrhea is usually concentrated in neonatal calves (20, 22). This discrepancy may be related to the unique husbandry system of yaks on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Unlike intensively raised dairy or beef calves, yaks are mainly managed under extensive grazing conditions, where adult animals may have more frequent exposure to contaminated pasture, water sources, and mixed-age herds. In addition, maternal antibody dynamics in yak calves may also influence the age distribution of BRV infection, while adult yaks may experience repeated exposure, nutritional stress, pregnancy or lactation stress, long-distance grazing, and harsh climatic conditions, which could increase susceptibility to infection or promote viral shedding. Therefore, the higher BRV positivity observed in adult yaks does not necessarily indicate that adults are more clinically susceptible to BRV-associated diarrhea than calves. Rather, it may reflect differences in exposure opportunity, immune status, and subclinical viral excretion under extensive grazing conditions. However, because this study included only diarrheic animals and lacked healthy controls, and because additional matched samples could not be collected for further confirmation, the relationship between age and clinical BRV disease should be interpreted cautiously and requires further validation.Seasonal variation was also observed in this study, with BRV positivity being lower in summer than in spring and winter (Figure 3E). This finding is consistent with the general epidemiological characteristics of enteric viruses, which can survive longer in colder environments (30, 31). In yak production areas, winter and spring are often associated with low temperature, limited forage availability, poor nutritional status, and increased physiological stress, all of which may reduce host resistance and facilitate viral transmission.
